page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring an x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon processor providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz and includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance bundles a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which provides 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy. Standard CPU and memory operations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25%, indicating weak general-purpose compute performance. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations show lower-tier performance. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for large language model inference. Prompt processing and text generation for both 135M and 7B parameter models rank in the top 10% of benchmarked systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 represents a specialized hardware profile where resource density is heavily weighted toward GPU acceleration rather than raw CPU power. It is highly optimized for workloads that can offload computation to the GPU, such as low-latency LLM inference, machine learning deployment, and graphics rendering. It is less suitable for CPU-bound tasks, heavy database operations, or workloads requiring high local storage IOPS due to the absence of local storage and lower CPU benchmark scores.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. The server's defining feature is a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 22 GB of VRAM. While standard CPU, memory, and database benchmarks place this instance in the lower performance tiers, its GPU-accelerated capabilities deliver top-tier results for machine learning tasks. Specifically, LLM inference speeds for prompt processing and text generation on 135M and 7B models rank in the top 10%. With no local storage included, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for specialized workloads that offload processing to the GPU. It is highly suited for AI inference, graphics rendering, and lightweight machine learning deployments, rather than general-purpose or CPU-heavy computing.
